findings.defect: The draft invents an unspecified plural actor and presents the line as external narration rather than Taekyung’s shocked realization that this is a forced opening.
findings.rationale: The Korean is a subjectless internal exclamation about the procedure itself; it does not identify multiple people as performing the action.

findings.current: I had never expected him to help me this much.
findings.defect: The translation preserves the extent of the help but omits 힘껏, which emphasizes how much effort and strength Jeok Cheongang expended.
findings.rationale: Jeok Cheongang’s exertion is meaningful characterization and directly supports the later revelation that the procedure consumed considerable internal energy and mental strength.
findings.replacement: To think he had gone all out to help me like this.

findings.defect: The draft turns an intentionally unfinished, emotional thought into a question about Jeok Cheongang’s identity or nature, creating a skeptical note absent from the source.
findings.rationale: The Korean trails off after addressing him, leaving Taekyung’s gratitude and emotion unspoken as his eyes grow moist.

findings.current: According to Childeuk, one of the martial artists at the training hall, Mukyung hadn’t come outside even once since entering.
findings.defect: The phrase “one of the martial artists” invents a group affiliation and blurs Childeuk’s specific role as the martial artist stationed at the training hall.
findings.rationale: The Korean identifies Childeuk by his particular post rather than as one member of an unspecified group.
findings.replacement: According to Childeuk, the martial artist stationed at the training hall, Mukyung hadn’t come outside even once since entering.
findings.source: 수련동 무인인 칠득이에 의하면 들어간 이래 단 한 번도 밖으로 나오지 않았다고 했다.

findings.current: “The Temple Master will feel just as sorry as you do, Lesser Family Head.”
findings.defect: “Feel sorry” suggests pity or apology, whereas 안타까워하다 here conveys regret or distress over Jin Mukyung’s decision.
findings.rationale: Ak Bulgun is saying that the Temple Master will share Jin Wikyung’s regret at Mukyung’s refusal to return, not that either man pities someone.
findings.replacement: “The Temple Master will regret it just as much as you do, Lesser Family Head.”

summary: The draft is broadly faithful, but it introduces a false plural subject during the forced opening, weakens Jeok Cheongang’s exertion, completes an intentionally unfinished thought, and contains two localized characterization issues.
